Commentary.Commentary: Now Sri Lanka will be under pressure! Ireland have got a big score on the board and Sri Lanka will need to replicate what they did with the bat in the first game. Ireland on the other hand, will need to be patient, bowl the right lines and lengths and hope the ball does do its bit. For now it is Tea so join us in a bit for the last session.

Sri Lanka toiled hard, it was not easy for their bowlers on a wicket which is quite flat and not doing a lot. They tried everything but wicket-taking was quite difficult for them. Yet again Prabath Jayasuriya who bowled almost 60 overs was the pick. The pacers also bowled their hearts out though as both got 4 amongst them.

Ireland fall just short of the 500-run mark but they will be very proud of their performance with the bat. The openers did not contribute a lot but the middle and the lower-middle order were brilliant. First it was two of their most experienced players who combined and laid the platform for a good first innings score. It was Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie! The two added over 100 before Paul Stirling went back retiered hurt. Andy Balbirnie was unfortunate to not get to his ton as he fell five short. Lorcan Tucker too played brilliantly but fell 20 short of a ton. However, then came the two tons for Ireland. One from Curtis Campher and another from Paul who resumed his innings. Ireland were eyeing 500 but wickets in the second session did not let them get there.

OUT! TKEN! That is the end of the innings for Ireland! Prabath Jayasuriya gets the last wicket and another fifer for him. Brilliant. Tosses this one up outside off, a lot slower. Matthew Humphreys looks to go down the ground but this lands and turns away. It goes off the outer half towards cover. Ramesh Mendis takes a decent catch. IRELAND END WITH 492!

This is a commendable job by Ireland. The way they batted in the first match and compare it to this match, there is a whole lot of difference in their character. Ireland lost Tucker right at the start of Day 2 but Paul Stirling came back fresh to build a big stand with Campher. Both hit the loose balls away regularly. Stirling got to his maiden Test century before giving away his wicket however, Campher is still batting brilliantly along with Andy McBrine and they will love to go past 450 in the next session. The last few overs saw the ball turning and bouncing and that will give some hope for Sri Lanka to take the remaining wickets quickly. Before that, they had to toil hard to earn their rewards. Not too many positives but they will eye the next session to finish things off. Stay tuned to find out what happens in the second session.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 between Ireland and Sri Lanka. The visitors finally produced with the bat as they dominated Day 1 thanks to the knock from their skipper and Stirling. Despite losing them, Ireland are in good position thanks to the stand between Tucker and Campher. Sri Lanka felt the pressure for the first time as they were not able to scalp wickets. Sri Lanka will hope to start Day 2 brightly and take remaining wickets quickly. Stay tuned.
...Day 2, Session 1...

Sri Lanka on the other hand, tried everything, They were made to work hard for the wickets they got. Their bowlers were not very consistent also with their lines and lengths. They bowled well in patches but there is not a lot on offer from the wicket. They will hope they can trigger a collapse on Day 2 and bowl Ireland out as quickly as possible. Day 2 begins at 1000 IST (0430 GMT). Till then, goodbye and take care!

It was Andy Balbirnie who led from the front. The openers were dismissed early, Tector got off to a staret but then fell, however, it was the partnership between Paul Stirling and Andy Balbirnie which laid the platform for a big first innings score. Both got to fifties and the partnership was over 100. Stirling then went back retired hurt but Andy Balbirnie continued along with Lorcan Tucker! The two put up another useful stand before Andy Balbirnie fell five short of a ton. Curtis Campher has come out and shown character. Ireland will hope they can bat for as long as possible as the wicket for now, seems really good.

An excellent, excellent day for the visitros and they will be extremely pleased with where they stand in the game at the moment. Two out of the three sessions have gone thier way. Andy Balbirnie's decision to bat first is justified for now.

Sri Lanka need to be patient with the ball, the wicket is quite flat and not offering a lot. They though will want to stop the run-flow a little and that might just build the pressure. Can Lanka make a come back in the last session?

Ireland lost two wickets quickly but Balbirnie started hitting boundaries regularly and raced away to his fifty in no time. A good stand was building with Tector but he gave away his wicket. For Sri Lanka, they will be happy too but could have done a lot better with the ball. Both the spinners especially as they will have a big session ahead and have to cut out the freebies they are giving regularly. Prabath Jayasuriya though has already got two wickets but Sri Lanka will hope for more from him and Ramesh Mendis. Stay tuned for the next session.

Hello and welcome to the second Test between Sri Lanka and Ireland. The Lankans have been unstoppable at home recently with their brilliant performance and it was seen yet again as they dominated the first match throughout. They had four centurions and after that, it was all spinners who did the job convincingly. Ireland will be disappointed with the effort but have a chance to rectify a few in this match. They need to bat with more character if they want to level the series. Not an easy task though. Can Sri Lanka clean sweep the series? We will find out. Toss and team news coming up.
